title: change owner: the queue-target check looks for a field named queue instead of a provisioned queue column, so an external object gets a queue write instead of the 400
body:
repo:objectstack#4 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5krBqrrgxCYgjXmfbv

Filing gate ① · Source: fleet · found by the #35270 review sweep (run records r04 S5, r03 N4) on PR #36154, re-read on main c30ce97cd7

## What happens
Change Owner can move a record into an ownership queue only if the object has queue storage. It decides that by looking for a field named `queue` in the object's definition, not by asking whether the column really exists in storage. So an external (federated) object that has an owner — where the platform lists a `queue` field but has no column for it — is sent a queue write instead of the documented "this object has no queue" refusal; and an object whose fields are registered as a list is refused with a sentence that is not true.

- `packages/core/src/security/change-record-owner.ts:213-218`: `asRecord(def.fields)` + `hasOwnProperty(fields, 'queue')`.
- The engine's own test is storage provenance: `packages/objectql/src/assignment-rules.ts:303-305` `carriesQueueColumn` = `resolveInjectedColumnProvenance(schema, 'queue') === 'injected-provisioned'`, used at `:332`, `:352`, `:621`.
- The injection plan registers `queue` wherever it registers `owner_id` (`packages/spec/src/data/injected-system-columns.ts:137-142`), so on a registered object the 400 arm practically never fires for the class that lacks storage.
- What the remote driver answers for the queue write was not traced.

## Done when
- The queue-target check uses the same provenance test as the engine (`carriesQueueColumn` or `resolveInjectedColumnProvenance(def, 'queue') === 'injected-provisioned'`), so array- and record-shaped `fields` answer alike.
- Pins: a federated object with an owner and an unprovisioned injected `queue` → 400 "no ownership queue column", no update call; an array-shaped `fields` registration with a provisioned queue → admitted; control: a local object with a provisioned queue → admitted.
- Ablation: restore the field-name test and the federated pin goes red.

reach: public HTTP doors `POST /api/v1/data/:object[/:id]/change-owner` with a `queue` target, on a writable external object that declares an owner, or an object registered with array-shaped fields. Read from the code, not measured.
Business reason: a queue hand-over on an external object should fail clearly; instead it is pushed to the remote system with an unknown result.
Reader: area:data / domain:server (packages/core security, change-owner).
Dedupe: `change owner`, `queue column`, `carriesQueueColumn` → no open card carries it.
Grade: p3 — narrow object class (external objects with an owner, or array-shaped registration).
